rationale.conceptual: The method relies on off-the-shelf Mol2vec embeddings and CATBoost regression/classification, with no original algorithm design. The domain-specific adaptation and careful validation (iSIM splitting, ensemble uncertainty) add moderate conceptual effort but remain within standard cheminformatics practice.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: data cleaning and iSIM-based splitting, Mol2vec featurization, separate model training for 7 properties with Optuna hyperparameter optimization, generation of at least 10,000 chemically valid ILs via RDKit, property prediction, and application of screening criteria. The orchestration involves several libraries and careful data handling, but no fragile multi-tool handoffs beyond standard ML workflows.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires implementing a standard machine learning pipeline using established embeddings (Mol2vec) and tree-based models (CATBoost) for property prediction, plus a downstream virtual screening. No novel algorithmic development; moderate conceptual depth in chemical representation and model validation. Execution involves multi-step data preprocessing, featurization, hyperparameter tuning, generation of chemically valid ILs, and screening — a moderately complex pipeline but manageable.

compute_estimate.reasoning: CATBoost is CPU-based and training on up to 52k samples with 300-dimensional embeddings is lightweight; Optuna hyperparameter tuning adds some overhead. The virtual screening of 10k ILs is trivial. Total data volume is modest.
